### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **23** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a095550a8295654918e69d29af7e202bc73742e1` — the merge of head `b7cf21da693d2bf13d74ea2dbca9fab14347e615` into base `1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a095550a8295654918e69d29af7e202bc73742e1 && git checkout a095550a8295654918e69d29af7e202bc73742e1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e b7cf21da693d2bf13d74ea2dbca9fab14347e615 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e && git merge --no-ff b7cf21da693d2bf13d74ea2dbca9fab14347e615

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1ff1d45d9bb670d4abf9097e99514205693b0b0e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

epic:#31527#1 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmP7o3uDTti21wLTfPf

**Epic red-line review — #31850 (#31790) at head 0dccea6c: CHANGES (two required, both on the approval half).**

**The assignment-rule half: PASS.** `assignment_rule` is `supportsOverlay: false`, `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false` and `allowRuntimeCreate: false` (spec `metadata-plugin.zod.ts:1307`). So no environment body of a rule exists, and the registry's `_packageId` is the package that declares it. An organization's `sys_assignment_rule` row is forced to `null`, which is the environment-wide read, as before. The service is the one resolver (#31789's contract). The rule never picks a holder itself.

**Your open questions**

1. *Clause-② "no (narrowing)" with two widening cases.* **Accepted.** D+U with P→D now reaching D, and P's own queue beside U, are D3's target answers: one holder in the closure, nothing guessed. This is the same reading as #31734/#31789's accepted widening. Keep both cases written out in the changeset, as they are now.
2. *A D3 refusal on an approval node reads `APPROVER_DIRECTORY_UNREADABLE`.* **Required fix (R2 below).** The candidates do reach the message (your "naming both" pin). The sentence around them is wrong for a refusal, though.
3. *Skills-docs follow-up.* Yes, the seat files it: Part of #31527, Blocked-by #31790, covering objectstack-automation SKILL.md and `state-machines-and-approvals.md`. It is a governed path and lands on maintainer approval.

**R1 (required): a step's package comes from the flow body that armed, not from the loader's set.**
`flowPackageOf` asks `packagedFlowOwner(flowName)`. That reads the artifact's `_packageId` for the bare name, so it answers P for every flow named after one of P's flows. It does so even when the body the engine runs is an environment-authored override of P's flow: a package-less stored row, or a declared override in P's `.custom` pair.
ADR-0150 D3 (the paragraph after (a)–(d)) says: *"A reference written in an environment-authored overlay (ADR-0005) is the environment's reference. It resolves as a caller with no package … It never resolves from the package the overlay customizes."*

With 0dccea6c, an administrator who edits P's approval step to name their own environment-authored queue is refused `outside-closure` (D3 (a)). That is a narrowing the changeset does not declare, and the ADR rules it out. An override that names a queue held by both D and U also resolves from P's closure instead of environment-wide.

Fix:
- Take the caller from the armed contender. A package body arms as `packageId`. An override or runtime body arms as `null`, which is no package.
- `getShadowedFlows()`/`armedFrom` is not enough as the source. It is recorded at boot and only on a collision. A runtime save of an override never writes it.
- The protocol already tells a served override row apart (`isServedOverrideRowOf`, `protocol-lock-state.ts`). Find the one fact the engine can be asked for the body it runs, measure it on a real kernel, and do not infer it from stamps: hydration grafts P's envelope onto the stored row, so `_packageId` on the body lies here.
- Pin it: P's flow overridden by a package-less row whose step names an environment-held queue must be served environment-wide, exactly as on main. Run that pin with the fix ablated (red), then with the fix (green).
- The decide-time tally (`process_name` `flow:…`) reads the same fact.

Card B #31696 rekeys flows by (package, name), and this obligation also goes on record there. Until B lands, this PR is the first to derive "the package of a flow step", and E5's last PR (connector_action connectorId by flow package) will copy whatever reading lands here. Please name the reader so that PR can reuse it.

**R2 (required): a refusal is not a failed read.**
When the cause is a `PackageScopedNameRefusedError`, the message says *"because a read behind it failed … Run the flow again once the directory can be read"*. Running the flow again changes nothing for an ambiguous or outside-closure name.
- Keep the node refusing, with the same class and the same no-route-past behaviour.
- When the cause is the D3 refusal, word it as a refused name and give the refusal's own remedy: declare the dependency, enable the package, or ship the queue in P.
- A new error code is a public name, so it is the seat's call. Rewording under the existing code is enough for this PR.
- Pin the remedy text in the "two holders in P's closure" case.

**Deviations noted, both fine:** plugin-approvals vitest `OS_REGISTRY_LOG`, and the objectql ablation.

Re-ping the epic seat with the new head once R1 and R2 are in.
